records.verificationNote: Both current Alabama Medicaid PDL documents (04/01/2026 Therapeutic-Category PDL and 07/01/2026 PDL Reference Tool, both fetched directly from medicaid.alabama.gov and keyword-searched in full) contain no oral-NSAID class entry (naproxen/ibuprofen/meloxicam/celecoxib/diclofenac). The only NSAID-adjacent hits are a topical/skin 'Nonsteroidal Anti-inflammatory Agents' line (Skin & Mucous Membrane section, generic-only, unrelated to oral use) and a narrow cardiovascular 'Nonsteroidal Anti-inflammatory Cardiovascular Drugs' entry for low-dose colchicine (Lodoco). Oral NSAIDs appear to be genuinely absent from AL Medicaid's brand-preferred/PA program, consistent with the source's opening statement that OTC and generic drugs are covered without prior approval 'unless otherwise specified' -- no oral NSAID is specified anywhere as an exception. Naproxen is presented here as a standard first-line, low-cost generic oral NSAID by clinical convention, not because the source names it.

records.verificationNote: Read pages 97-98 (printed pages 89-90) of the PDF, ANALGESICS - ANTI-INFLAMMATORY section, position-parsed. Naproxen (both 'naproxen tab' and 'naproxen sodium tab'), ibuprofen, meloxicam, celecoxib, and diclofenac sodium/potassium are all Tier 1 with zero flags in every restriction column. The only PA-flagged items in this section are the fixed-dose GI-protective combination products (Vimovo, Duexis), not core single-agent NSAIDs.
